title: First and Last Occurrence
description:
You are given a list of n integers sorted in non-decreasing order and q query values. For each query value, find the 0-based index of its first and last occurrence in the list. If the value does not occur, the answer is -1 -1. Aim for O(log n) per query (binary search).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 2000
  • -109 ≤ values ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: q. Line 4: q query integers.

Output

For each query, in the given order, print one line first last separated by a single space.

Example

Input:

8
1 2 2 2 3 5 5 8
3
2 5 4

Output:

1 3
5 6
-1 -1
solution:
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
q = int(input())
qs = list(map(int, input().split()))
out = []
for x in qs:
    l = bisect_left(a, x)
    if l < n and a[l] == x:
        out.append(f"{l} {bisect_right(a, x) - 1}")
    else:
        out.append("-1 -1")
print("\n".join(out))

title: Search in a Rotated Sorted Array
description:
An array of n distinct integers was sorted in ascending order and then rotated at some unknown pivot (for example [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] may become [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]; a rotation by 0 leaves it unchanged). For each of q query values, print its 0-based index in the rotated array, or -1 if it is absent. Use a modified binary search (O(log n) per query).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 2000
  • |values| ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: the rotated array. Line 3: q. Line 4: q queries.

Output

One line per query containing the index or -1.

Example

Input:

7
4 5 6 7 0 1 2
4
0 3 4 2

Output:

4
-1
0
6

title: Find the First Peak
description:
An element of an array is a peak if it is strictly greater than each of its existing neighbours (the elements just before and after it; positions outside the array are treated as negative infinity). Print the smallest 0-based index of a peak, or -1 if the array has no peak (this can only happen when equal values are present).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 104
  • |ai| ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

A single integer: the index of the first peak, or -1.

Example

Input:

5
1 3 2 4 1

Output:

1
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ans = -1
for i in range(n):
    left = a[i - 1] if i > 0 else None
    right = a[i + 1] if i + 1 < n else None
    if (left is None or a[i] > left) and (right is None or a[i] > right):
        ans = i
        break
print(ans)

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description:
Koko has n piles of bananas and h hours. Each hour she picks one pile and eats k bananas from it; if the pile has fewer than k bananas she eats them all and does nothing else that hour. Find the minimum integer speed k that lets her finish all piles within h hours. Binary search on the answer.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, n ≤ h ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ pile ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n h. Line 2: n pile sizes.

Output

The minimum speed k.

Example

Input:

4 8
3 6 7 11

Output:

4

title: Aggressive Cows
description:
A barn has n stalls at distinct positions on a line (given in no particular order). You must place c cows in different stalls so that the minimum distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Print that largest possible minimum distance. Brute force over placements is far too slow; sort and binary search on the answer with a greedy check.

  • 2 ≤ c ≤ n ≤ 2000
  • 0 ≤ position ≤ 109, all distinct

Input

Line 1: n c. Line 2: n stall positions.

Output

The largest minimum distance.

Example

Input:

5 3
1 2 8 4 9

Output:

3

title: Kth Largest Element
description:
Given n integers and an integer k, print the k-th largest element. Duplicates count separately (in [3,3,2] the 2nd largest is 3).

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 104
  • |ai| ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n k. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The k-th largest value.

Example

Input:

6 2
3 2 1 5 6 4

Output:

5
solution:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = sorted(map(int, input().split()), reverse=True)
print(a[k - 1])

title: Sort Words by Length Then Alphabet
description:
Sort n lowercase words primarily by length (shorter first) and, for equal lengths, in lexicographic (dictionary) order. Duplicate words are kept.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
  • Each word has 1 to 20 lowercase letters.

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: one word each.

Output

The sorted words, one per line.

Example

Input:

5
banana
kiwi
apple
fig
date

Output:

fig
date
kiwi
apple
banana
solution:
n = int(input())
ws = [input().strip() for _ in range(n)]
ws.sort(key=lambda w: (len(w), w))
print("\n".join(ws))

title: Multi-Key Student Ranking
description:
Each student record contains a name, an integer age and an integer score. Sort the records by:

  • score descending, then
  • age ascending, then
  • name ascending (ordinary case-sensitive string comparison, so uppercase letters come before lowercase ones).

Records that are completely identical are all kept.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000; names are non-empty and contain no spaces; 0 ≤ age, score ≤ 1000

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: name age score.

Output

The sorted records, one per line, formatted name age score.

Example

Input:

4
Ana 20 90
Ben 19 90
Cara 19 95
Dan 19 90

Output:

Cara 19 95
Ben 19 90
Dan 19 90
Ana 20 90
solution:
n = int(input())
rs = []
for _ in range(n):
    name, age, score = input().split()
    rs.append((name, int(age), int(score)))
rs.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[2], r[1], r[0]))
for name, age, score in rs:
    print(name, age, score)

title: Largest Concatenated Number
description:
Arrange n non-negative integers so that, written next to each other, they form the largest possible number. Print that number as a string. The result must not have unnecessary leading zeros: if every value is 0, print just 0.

Hint: ordinary numeric or string sorting is wrong (compare 3 and 30, or 824 and 8247); compare two strings a, b by which of a+b and b+a is bigger.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 1500, 0 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The largest number.

Example

Input:

5
3 30 34 5 9

Output:

9534330
solution:
from functools import cmp_to_key
n = int(input())
a = input().split()
a = [str(int(x)) for x in a]
a.sort(key=cmp_to_key(lambda x, y: (x + y < y + x) - (x + y > y + x)))
s = "".join(a).lstrip("0")
print(s if s else "0")

title: Activity Selection
description:
There are n activities, each with a start time s and finish time f (s < f). One person can do one activity at a time; an activity may start at exactly the moment the previous one finishes. Print the maximum number of activities that can be performed.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ s < f ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: s f.

Output

The maximum number of activities.

Example

Input:

6
1 2
3 4
0 6
5 7
8 9
5 9

Output:

4
solution:
n = int(input())
iv = [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
iv.sort(key=lambda p: p[1])
cnt, end = 0, -1
for s, f in iv:
    if s >= end:
        cnt += 1
        end = f
print(cnt)

title: Fractional Knapsack
description:
A thief has a bag of capacity W and there are n items, each with a value v and a weight w. Any fraction of an item may be taken (taking a fraction x of an item gives x·v value and uses x·w capacity). Print the maximum total value that fits, rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ W ≤ 106
  • 0 ≤ v ≤ 104, 1 ≤ w ≤ 104

Input

Line 1: n W. Next n lines: v w.

Output

The maximum value with 2 decimals, e.g. 240.00.

Example

Input:

3 50
60 10
100 20
120 30

Output:

240.00
solution:
n, W = map(int, input().split())
items = [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
items.sort(key=lambda t: t[0] / t[1], reverse=True)
total = 0.0
cap = W
for v, w in items:
    if cap <= 0:
        break
    take = min(w, cap)
    total += v * take / w
    cap -= take
print(f"{total:.2f}")

title: Minimum Railway Platforms
description:
Given the arrival and departure times (in minutes after midnight) of n trains for one day, find the minimum number of platforms so that no train waits. A train occupies its platform from its arrival minute to its departure minute inclusive: if one train arrives at the same minute another departs, they need different platforms. Train i's departure is never earlier than its arrival.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ arrival ≤ departure ≤ 1439

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n arrival times. Line 3: n departure times (the i-th departure belongs to the i-th arrival).

Output

The minimum number of platforms.

Example

Input:

6
900 940 950 1100 1430 1000
910 1200 1120 1130 1439 1000

Output:

3
solution:
n = int(input())
arr = sorted(map(int, input().split()))
dep = sorted(map(int, input().split()))
i = j = cur = best = 0
while i < n:
    if arr[i] <= dep[j]:
        cur += 1
        i += 1
        best = max(best, cur)
    else:
        cur -= 1
        j += 1
print(best)

title: Gas Station Circuit
description:
There are n gas stations on a circular route, numbered 0 to n-1. Station i gives gas[i] units of fuel, and driving from station i to station (i+1) mod n costs cost[i] units. You start with an empty tank (unlimited capacity) at some station, fill up there, and must travel once around the circuit back to it; the tank may never go negative. Print the smallest starting index that works, or -1 if none does.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 104, 0 ≤ gas[i], cost[i] ≤ 104

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: gas values. Line 3: cost values.

Output

The smallest valid starting index, or -1.

Example

Input:

5
1 2 3 4 5
3 4 5 1 2

Output:

3
solution:
n = int(input())
g = list(map(int, input().split()))
c = list(map(int, input().split()))
P = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    P[i + 1] = P[i] + g[i] - c[i]
total = P[n]
INF = float("inf")
suf = [INF] * (n + 2)
for m in range(n, 0, -1):
    suf[m] = min(suf[m + 1], P[m])
ans = -1
if total >= 0:
    pre = INF
    for i in range(n):
        # trips not wrapping: P[m]-P[i] for m in i+1..n ; wrapping: total+P[m]-P[i] for m in 1..i
        if suf[i + 1] - P[i] >= 0 and (pre == INF or total + pre - P[i] >= 0):
            ans = i
            break
        pre = min(pre, P[i + 1])
print(ans)

title: Jump Game Reachability
description:
You stand at index 0 of an array of non-negative integers. The value at each index is the maximum jump length from that position (you may jump any distance from 0 up to it). Print YES if you can reach the last index, otherwise NO.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 104, 0 ≤ ai ≤ 105

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

YES or NO.

Example

Input:

5
2 3 1 1 4

Output:

YES
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
far = 0
for i in range(n):
    if i > far:
        break
    far = max(far, i + a[i])
print("YES" if far >= n - 1 else "NO")

description:
Each child i has a greed factor g[i]: the minimum cookie size that will content them. Each cookie j has a size s[j]. Each child gets at most one cookie and each cookie goes to at most one child. Print the maximum number of content children.

  • 1 ≤ number of children, cookies ≤ 3000
  • 1 ≤ g[i], s[j] ≤ 106

Line 1: number of children. Line 2: greed factors. Line 3: number of cookies. Line 4: cookie sizes.

Output

The maximum number of content children.

Input:

3
1 2 3
2
1 1

Output:

1
solution:
input()
g = sorted(map(int, input().split()))
input()
s = sorted(map(int, input().split()))
i = 0
for x in s:
    if i < len(g) and x >= g[i]:
        i += 1
print(i)

title: Minimum Arrows to Burst Balloons
description:
Balloons are taped to a wall; balloon i spans horizontal coordinates x1 to x2 (inclusive). An arrow shot vertically at coordinate x bursts every balloon with x1 ≤ x ≤ x2 (touching an endpoint counts). Print the minimum number of arrows needed to burst all balloons.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, -109 ≤ x1 ≤ x2 ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: x1 x2.

Output

The minimum number of arrows.

Example

Input:

4
10 16
2 8
1 6
7 12

Output:

2
solution:
n = int(input())
iv = sorted((tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)), key=lambda p: p[1])
arrows, pos = 0, None
for a, b in iv:
    if pos is None or a > pos:
        arrows += 1
        pos = b
print(arrows)

title: Job Sequencing with Deadlines
description:
There are n jobs. Job i takes exactly one unit of time, has a deadline d and a profit p; it earns its profit only if it is completed by time d, i.e. scheduled in one of the time slots 1, 2, ..., d. Only one job can run per slot. Choose a schedule that maximises total profit, then print the number of jobs in it and the total profit.

Deadlines can be as large as 109, so a slot array is impossible; and n is large enough that an O(n·d) or exponential search is too slow. (With all profits positive, every maximum-profit schedule contains the same number of jobs.)

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ d ≤ 109, 1 ≤ p ≤ 106

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: d p.

Output

Two integers separated by a space: the number of scheduled jobs and the maximum total profit.

Example

Input:

4
4 20
1 10
1 40
1 30

Output:

2 60
solution:
import heapq
n = int(input())
js = sorted(tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n))
h = []
for d, p in js:
    heapq.heappush(h, p)
    if len(h) > d:
        heapq.heappop(h)
print(len(h), sum(h))

title: Minimum Cost to Merge Ropes
description:
You have n ropes with given lengths. Joining two ropes of lengths x and y produces one rope of length x+y and costs x+y. Any two ropes may be joined (not only neighbours). Print the minimum total cost to join all ropes into one (this is the Huffman merge cost). With a single rope the cost is 0.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 1 ≤ length ≤ 106

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n lengths.

Output

The minimum total cost.

Example

Input:

4
4 3 2 6

Output:

29
solution:
import heapq
n = int(input())
h = list(map(int, input().split()))
heapq.heapify(h)
cost = 0
while len(h) > 1:
    s = heapq.heappop(h) + heapq.heappop(h)
    cost += s
    heapq.heappush(h, s)
print(cost)

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description:
Split an array of n non-negative integers into exactly k non-empty contiguous parts so that the largest part sum is as small as possible. Print that minimum possible largest sum. Trying all cut positions is exponential; binary search on the answer with a greedy feasibility check (or DP) is required.

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ ai ≤ 106

Input

Line 1: n k. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The minimised largest part sum.

Example

Input:

5 2
7 2 5 10 8

Output:

18

title: Counting Sort with Negatives
description:
Sort n integers in the range -1000..1000 in ascending order using counting sort (count how many times each value appears, then output the values in order). Then, on a second line, print the value that appears most often; if several values tie, print the smallest of them.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000, -1000 ≤ ai ≤ 1000

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

Line 1: the sorted values separated by single spaces. Line 2: the most frequent value (smallest on ties).

Example

Input:

6
4 -1 2 4 0 -1

Output:

-1 -1 0 2 4 4
-1
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
cnt = [0] * 2001
for x in a:
    cnt[x + 1000] += 1
out = []
for i in range(2001):
    out.extend([str(i - 1000)] * cnt[i])
print(" ".join(out))
best = max(cnt)
print(cnt.index(best) - 1000)
